info.title: OpenAsy Profiling API
info.summary: Which functions use the CPU and memory, all the time, in production: profiles kept in Pyroscope, read as flame graphs and compared.
info.description:
Every screen of Profiling uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Profiles are pushed with `PROFILING_INGEST_TOKEN` or an API token with the editor role: Grafana Alloy's `pyroscope.write`, which its eBPF profiler `pyroscope.ebpf` sends to, posts to `/push.v1.PusherService/Push`, and the Pyroscope SDKs to `/ingest`. Profiling also reads pprof from the pull targets people add. Pyroscope's query API is answered under `/querier.v1.QuerierService/` as Pyroscope answers it, for Grafana's Pyroscope data source with an API token of the viewer role. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description: Pyroscope's push API, which Alloy's `pyroscope.write` posts to with the address `https://profiling.example.com`: its eBPF profiler (`pyroscope.ebpf`), `pyroscope.java` and `pyroscope.scrape` all send through it. Connect over HTTP, protobuf or JSON. With `PROFILING_INGEST_TOKEN`, or an API token with the editor role.

400.description: The body could not be read, with why.

422.description: Pyroscope refused the profile, with why.

post.description: Pyroscope's ingest API, as its SDKs and agents send to it: `?name=service{label=value}&format=pprof` (or jfr, folded and the other formats it reads), the profile in the body. With `PROFILING_INGEST_TOKEN`, or an API token with the editor role.

400.description: The body could not be read, with why.

422.description: Pyroscope refused the profile, with why.

post.description: Needs the viewer role. Passed to Pyroscope as it is, for Grafana's Pyroscope data source: ProfileTypes, LabelNames, LabelValues, Series, SelectMergeStacktraces, SelectMergeSpanProfile, SelectMergeProfile, SelectSeries, Diff and GetProfileStats. Its other services are not reachable.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Profiling runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Profiling origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_profiling_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003). Grafana sends one as its data source's bearer token.

adminToken.description: Only when Profiling is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `PROFILING_INGEST_TOKEN`: for Grafana Alloy and the Pyroscope SDKs. It can push profiles, nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

unit.description: Of every value: nanoseconds, bytes or count.

targetId.description: The pull target its profiles come from; null when they are pushed.

labels.description: Each label of the service's profiles in the period, with its values.

name.description: The function; total for the root.

total.description: Value of the stacks through it, in the type's unit.

self.description: Value of the stacks that end in it.

total.description: Counted once when it calls itself.
Value of every stack in the period, in the type's unit.

functions.description: The 100 functions with the most self value.

baseSelf.description: Share of the baseline's value spent in the function itself, in percent.

change.description: headSelf - baseSelf, in percentage points; above 0 it takes more than it did.

functions.description: At most 200, the ones that moved most first.

bytes.description: Size of the profile as the target sent it.

service.description: The service_name its profiles are stored under.

url.description: The pprof address; each type is read at a path under it.

intervalSeconds.description: How often it is read; null reads it only on demand.

hasSecret.description: Whether a password or bearer token is kept. It is never returned (ADR 0021).

url.description: http:// or https://, such as http://10.0.0.5:6060/debug/pprof; one without a path reads /debug/pprof.

types.description: cpu reads /profile?seconds=cpuSeconds; the others read /heap, /goroutine, /mutex and /block.

labels.description: At most 10, such as version or env; not service_name.

secret.description: The bearer token or password, sealed with the install's key. Leave it out to keep the one kept.

type.description: One of the target's types; its first by default.

services.description: Services with profiles in the last hour.

failing.description: Targets whose last capture failed, at most 20.

ConnectAnswer.description: Pyroscope's own answer, as its Connect API writes it: JSON or protobuf, as the request asked.
